what_happened: The job to link the producer's CARGO_TARGET_DIR to the slot's warm target dir was rejected at the final verdict. There were three major findings and no blockers. No acceptance criteria are listed as unmet and no checks are listed as failed. First, the new tests in slot_exec.rs write an executable (bin/cargo) and run it in-process, which is the ETXTBSY race the repository forbids in test code, and the suite was flaky and failed during verification. Second, the wrapper links the slot but never runs the workspace-output clean that the scheme requires after each command, so the producer's workspace-crate output builds up in the shared slot. Third, the accepted reading did not match the request, so passing criteria did not show the request was met.
cause: The reading was accepted without being cross-checked against the request or against the scheme the request relies on. The scheme requires a workspace-output clean after each command. The reading's criteria checked that the link exists, not that the scheme's cleanup happens, so a wrapper that only half implements the scheme still passed them. Separately, the known ETXTBSY rule for tests that write and run executables is not shown to the producer. Nothing scans the diff for that pattern before the verifier. Both gaps were found only when the verifier read the finished diff.
prevention: Two checks would have prevented the class. (1) Before a reading is accepted, a step compares it with the request and with the named scheme or decision it depends on, lists every required behavior (here, link plus clean after each command), and makes each one a behavior criterion, so the reading cannot drop one. (2) A pre-verification code scan flags tests that write a file, set it executable and run it in-process. The producer is told the repo's approved pattern for stand-in executables, so the ETXTBSY race is caught before the verifier sees it.
proposed_request: Make the producer's cargo builds use the slot's warm target directory. Outcome: when a producer runs cargo through the slot wrapper in crates/athena-cli/src/slot_exec.rs, CARGO_TARGET_DIR points at the slot's warm target dir, and after each command the wrapper runs the workspace-output clean the slot scheme requires, so the producer's workspace-crate output does not build up in the shared slot. Acceptance: (1) a test shows that a run through the wrapper sets CARGO_TARGET_DIR to the slot's warm target dir; (2) a test shows that after the command finishes, the workspace-crate output is removed from the slot while the warm dependency artifacts remain; (3) the cleanup also runs when the command fails; (4) tests do not write and then execute a freshly created executable in-process, using the repository's approved ETXTBSY-safe pattern for stand-in scripts instead; (5) the changelog and any affected decision record match what the diff does. Before writing the reading, read the slot scheme in docs/decisions.md and restate each behavior it requires of the wrapper.
